key_insight: Partially miscible mass transfer in two-phase porous-media displacement is mainly stabilizing, reducing viscous fingering growth and especially suppressing upward gravity-driven instabilities.
engineering_relevance: This matters for enhanced oil recovery, CO2 sequestration, and groundwater remediation because it helps predict when interphase mass transfer can improve front stability and displacement efficiency.
method: Formulate a linear stability eigenvalue problem for two-phase, two-component flow with gravity, fractional flow, capillarity, dispersion, and mass transfer.
Derive jump conditions to handle discontinuous coefficients at the two-phase to pure-liquid transition.
Solve the eigenproblem with a matched initial value problem method to obtain growth rates and cutoff wavenumbers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical stability results showing mass transfer lowers perturbation growth rates most strongly, with a weaker effect on cutoff wavenumber, and identifies a critical dispersion coefficient where both are maximized.
watch_item: The analysis is linear and idealized, so real porous-media systems with nonlinear effects, heterogeneity, and uncertain interphase transfer may deviate from the predicted stability trends.
paper_title: Linear Stability Analysis of Two-phase, Two-Component Flow in Porous Media
